dimensions.assessment: Involves federal financial and intelligence agencies (Treasury, FinCEN, Department of Justice, DNI) and congressional committees.
dimensions.evidence: the Secretary of the Treasury shall submit to the Committee on Financial Services of the House of Representatives and the Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs of the Senate a report

dimensions.assessment: Mandates administrative reporting on data collections and annual review of protocols to protect privacy rights, with a 7-year sunset provision.
dimensions.evidence: In consultation with the Director of National Intelligence and the Attorney General, the Secretary of the Treasury shall annually review and, as appropriate, revise any written protocols

dimensions.assessment: No federal spending or economic impact amounts are stated in the source text.
Amends chapter 53 of title 31, United States Code, to establish a new reporting requirement and annual review protocol for financial data access.
dimensions.evidence: Chapter 53 of title 31, United States Code, is amended... by inserting after section 5326 the following: Sec. 5327. Reports to Congress

dimensions.assessment: Temporary duration lasting for a 7-year period beginning on the date of enactment before a sunset takes effect.
dimensions.evidence: On the date that is the end of the 7-year period beginning on the date of enactment of this Act-- (1) section 5327 of title 31, United States Code, is repealed

missing_information: Cost estimates or resource requirements for preparing the annual congressional reports and interagency reviews.
importance_detail.rationale: Requires the Department of the Treasury to submit annual reports to Congress regarding Bank Secrecy Act reports and agency access protocols, and to annually review these protocols with other agencies.
